text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The General manager of Harare Sheraton Klaus Gurney's contract has expired and his future at the hotel was still not clear early this week.

- In what could be Zimbabwe's largest investment in neighbouring Mozambique, Chibuku Regional Investments is setting up a multi-million dollar brewery plant in the town of Chimoio which will see the creation of at least 70 new jobs.

- President Robert Mugabe said on Wednesday the government would foster a conducive macro-economic environment to consolidate the gains of the first phase of the country's economic reform programme as it entered the second phase.
- National Railways of Zimbabwe workers went on strike on Wednesday over salary increment disputes, joining construction and clothing industry employees who downed tools earlier in the week.

- Former army chief General Solomon Mujuru, ordered by President Robert Mugabe to withdraw from a deal in which he bought a part of smelting company ZIMASCO, is refusing to surrender his multi-million dollar stake. Top company officials have asked the president to intervene.

- Air Zimbabwe chief executive Brendon Donohoe has asked President Robert Mugabe to use the airline's scheduled flights on his overseas trips in an effort to minimise disruptions to the airline's operations.

- Finance ministry officials said they were launching a probe into charges that urban state land was being sold on a preferential basis to top government officials and private citizens in selected low-density suburbs of Harare.

- The government, facing mounting protests by war veterans demanding lump sum payments from Zimbabwe's War Victims Compensation Fund, said on Wednesday it was resuming disbursements from the fund. It suspended payments in March after charges that the money had been abused by top-ranking government officials.
